column3: The Hebrew describes residing as a stranger in the “fields of Moab”; BSB uses “reside in the land of Moab.”
The Hebrew repeats “name” for the man, his wife, and his two sons, with singular “name” for the two sons together. It calls Moab’s territory “fields,” rendered “land” in BSB.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they lived “there”; BSB explicitly supplies “in Moab.”
The Hebrew calls her “the woman”; BSB identifies her as Naomi.
The Hebrew first says that she rose and returned, then explains what she had heard. BSB puts her hearing first and describes her as preparing to leave; it renders “bread” as “food.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers simply to “the dead”; BSB adds the possessive “your.”
The Hebrew says they “lifted their voice and wept”; BSB combines these actions into “wept aloud.” It adds “new” to the husband.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew commands “return” without an explicit “home”; BSB supplies “home.”
The Hebrew has no separate adjective for “another” husband or explicit destination “home.” It introduces the possibility with “if I said,” rendered “if I thought” in BSB.
The Hebrew describes her condition as “very bitter”; BSB renders this as “it grieves me very much.” It repeats “for them” in both questions, which BSB states only in the first.
The Hebrew says they “lifted their voice and wept” again; BSB has “wept aloud.” The kiss has no separate word corresponding to “goodbye.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and repeats “your sister-in-law” in the return command. BSB supplies Naomi and replaces the second sister-in-law with “her.”
The Hebrew uses the verb for spending the night; BSB renders it as “live.” The statements “your people, my people” and “your God, my God” contain no explicit future verb.
The Hebrew’s oath literally says “thus may the LORD do to me, and thus may He add”; BSB makes the punishment and its severity explicit. BSB also supplies “anything but” before death.
The Hebrew leaves both women unnamed and says she stopped speaking to her. BSB supplies Naomi and Ruth and specifies that she stopped “trying to persuade her.”
The Hebrew says “the two of them,” where BSB supplies Naomi and Ruth. The speakers are marked by a feminine plural verb; BSB explicitly identifies them as “the women of the city.”
